## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: no-passing zones, roundabouts, diverging diamonds and parking
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from this section's selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge or memory.
The first selected page opens with the end of a passing-on-the-right condition that began on the previous page; that condition is not restated here because it spans two pages [A01].
The diverging diamond text on the second selected page is out of reading order in the extracted text; each rule was taught only where its sentence could be rebuilt without guessing [A02].
The roundabout sentences at the top of the second selected page appear to be a figure caption; they were used only where they repeat the yield rule [A02].
The hill-parking figure on the last selected page is an image with three labels; the wheel positions were taken from the printed paragraph, not the drawing [A03].
Originality: every statement is reworded from the cited page; no manual sentence, table, image or official test question is reproduced.
Exam numbers: the manual prints no question count, passing score, item format or time limit, so none is stated anywhere in this section; the typed debts live in part A.
External review: restating published Arizona traffic and licensing rules needs no clinical or legal sign-off; none is requested.

corpus_stability.reason: The Arizona Driver License Manual carries one revision line on its contents page (Revised September 2026) and points to Arizona Revised Statutes Title 28 for current law; nothing in the selected pages signals more than one rewrite per year.

verification_debt.claim_text: The manual says parking in an accessible space without a valid placard or plate may result in a fine but gives no amount; confirm any amount from Arizona Revised Statutes before teaching it.
